title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, fully archived, verifier‑grounded comparison between a deterministic template baseline and a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. A deterministic open validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) produced binary verifier pass/fail judgments on each generated configuration. Confirmatory paired analysis (N = 120 pairs) found baseline success = 120/120 and gpt‑5‑mini guarded success = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Artifact provenance shows the confirmatory runs used preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (the same canonical candidate was supplied to both conditions per pair for seed_0). We therefore interpret the degenerate (perfect‑agreement) outcome as an artifact‑grounded fact about this preregistered pipeline and document why it does not imply operational equivalence. We release the full execution and analysis bundle and specify concrete next steps required to evaluate independent model generation under realistic NetOps diversity.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration to accelerate network operations. Operational correctness requires semantic properties (reachability, ACL/BGP policy preservation, change ordering) that token‑level metrics do not capture. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 to produce an auditable, verifier‑grounded paired comparison between (A) a deterministic template baseline and (B) an LLM single‑pass generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. Research question: under a preregistered, artifact‑archived protocol, does a single‑pass LLM generator yield a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline (paired analysis)? Contributions: (1) a fully archived, preregistered confirmatory run with every model call and validator trace (preregistration SHA‑256: 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37); (2) deterministic, artifact‑grounded diagnosis of a degenerate confirmatory outcome arising from preregistered generation semantics, with exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for audit; (3) concrete, artifact‑backed recommendations for verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation (independent generation semantics, multi‑seed sampling, diverse tasks, multiple validator modalities).
sections.related_work: LLM‑assisted intent→configuration and generate–validate–repair patterns have been studied alongside network configuration verifiers (Batfish, control‑plane analyzers) that expose semantic failures invisible to surface metrics [1–3]. Prior work emphasizes verifier grounding and iterative repair; our novelty is a preregistered, artifact‑anchored confirmatory experiment with fully archived prompts, responses, and validator traces enabling reproducible audit and failure diagnosis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: the preregistered plan (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1, SHA‑256 7db1663c...) specified: task bank N=120 (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS); two conditions (baseline, guarded); primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sampling: one canonical seed (seed_0) per task; exploratory plan: additional seeds for seed‑sensitivity (not used for the primary confirmatory inference). Execution and models: declared_model_version=gpt‑5‑mini via provider adapter 'openai_responses' and adapter family 'hosted_netops_gvr_v1' (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) computed normalized configuration, applied intent constraints, and produced binary pass/fail and detailed validator_trace for each episode (execution/scoring/*). Confirmatory generation semantics: the preregistered execution used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" for the seed_0 confirmatory runs; consequently the same canonical candidate was supplied to both baseline and guarded scoring episodes per pair. Representative artifacts proving shared_initial usage: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...) and execution/responses/task-000002-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 ae967f70dfb6ccb8b5...). Execution accounting and reproducibility: execution/execution_manifest.json records completed_episode_count = 240 and model_calls_used = 120 (preregistered maximum_model_calls = 240); full hash manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 are archived (execution/*). Contamination heuristics: preregistered string‑overlap rules (exact match or normalized 5‑gram ≥ 0.95 flagged suspected_contamination; normalized Levenshtein ≥ 0.90 flagged high_overlap) were computed; analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA‑256 389227f0...) contains results.
sections.results: All confirmatory pairs completed (complete_pairs = 120) with no infrastructure failures. Validator outcomes: baseline successes = 120/120 (100%); guarded (gpt‑5‑mini seed_0) successes = 120/120 (100%). Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Paired estimator = 0.00. Bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative archived episode (task‑000001) shows identical shared_initial candidate and identical scored outputs for both conditions (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), with validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true. Deterministic reconciliation checks passed (deterministic_reconciliation.json archived; all accounting checks true).
sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded interpretation. The confirmatory null result (zero paired difference) is an accurate, artifact‑backed description of the preregistered run, but it does not demonstrate equivalence between independent template baselines and independent LLM generation. Three artifact‑documented facts explain this: (1) Shared‑initial candidate semantics — the confirmatory seed_0 runs used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" so both conditions were evaluated on identical canonical candidates per pair (evidence: execution/responses/* shared‑initial files and execution/execution_manifest.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...); (2) Validator–task coupling — the deterministic task‑synthesis/transformation pipeline encoded the same required_sequence and intent constraints that the validator enforces (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and transformation_manifest.json entries), increasing the chance that template‑aligned candidates validate; (3) Templated synthetic tasks — the programmatic task bank is constrained and unit‑tested, favoring regular solution forms. Together these factors create a confirmatory design that legitimately measures verifier outcomes on supplied canonical candidates, not independent model generative robustness. Evidence‑to‑claim mapping (select examples): claim 'shared_initial was used' → execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), claim 'paired contingency n_11 = 120' → analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 9f25790c...), claim 'validator trace shows valid final_state for task‑000001' → execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...). Implications for NetOps evaluation: verifier grounding remains necessary; confirmatory designs must ensure independence between compared generators (do not supply identical canonical candidates across conditions), include multi‑seed sampling, broaden task heterogeneity (less templated), and use multiple validator modalities (control‑plane emulator, reachability analyzers) to probe realistic failure modes. All recommended next‑step actions are reproducible from the archived artifacts and can be executed by re‑running the archived code with alternate execution semantics (e.g., independent LLM sampling per condition).
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic confirmatory protocol, both the deterministic template baseline and the recorded gpt‑5‑mini single‑pass guarded condition produced verifier‑valid configurations on the N=120 synthetic tasks (both 120/120). The degenerate result is artifact‑grounded and attributable to preregistered generation semantics and templated tasks; it therefore does not generalize to independent LLM generation in open operational distributions. We release the full execution and analysis artifacts to enable reproducible follow‑ups and recommend that future verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluations adopt independent generation semantics, multi‑seed sampling, diverse task banks, and multiple validators to assess operational reliability more broadly.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track). LLM(s) and provider: declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini accessed via provider adapter 'openai_responses' and adapter family 'hosted_netops_gvr_v1' (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Orchestration and framework: autonomous execution used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and deterministic scoring via deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Preregistration: CAND-2026-001-NetConfig-Semantic-v1 was frozen prior to execution; preregistration SHA‑256: 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37. Initial master prompt: immutable reference provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) is included in the artifact bundle and cited here as the exact immutable prompt reference. Human role and autonomy boundary: the Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI system autonomously performed literature review, research‑gap selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, deterministic validation, statistical analysis, autonomous internal peer review, and manuscript drafting and revision. No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Confirmatory generation semantics and provenance (explicit, artifact‑backed): the preregistered confirmatory runs used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate"; the execution record shows that for each confirmatory pair the same canonical shared_initial candidate was supplied to both the baseline and guarded scoring episodes (representative artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36..., execution/responses/task-000002-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 ae967f70dfb6ccb8b5...). As a result, the confirmatory paired comparison measured verifier outcomes on identical canonical candidates per pair rather than independent generator outputs; this fact is explicitly documented in Methods, Results, and Discussion and proven by the archived artifacts. Contamination detection: preregistered string‑overlap heuristics were computed (exact‑match or normalized 5‑gram overlap ≥ 0.95 flagged as 'suspected_contamination', normalized Levenshtein ≥ 0.90 flagged as 'high_overlap'); the confirmatory set produced no flags (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0d1e8...). Validator artifacts and representative scoring files: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57fff893fe02bd395c435a422f5431376e439875577a8431063) and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 9f25790c7eeaafb3562e0710e0cf10b7a47a55ea00fcbcf02eee324f79afafe7) are provided to enable independent audit. Retry and failure policy: preregistered retry rules allowed up to two automatic retries for infrastructure failures; no such retries were required (execution/execution_manifest.json). Limitations: the manuscript documents (and the artifacts confirm) that (1) shared_initial generation semantics reduce independence between conditions; (2) the deterministic validator enforces the same constraints used by the task synthesis pipeline; (3) tasks were programmatically templated and unit‑tested; (4) single canonical seed for the confirmatory test limits seed‑sensitivity assessment; (5) training‑data exposure cannot be proven absent external model training logs, though contamination heuristics were run and archived. Full artifact release: the complete execution and analysis bundle (execution/*, analysis/*, deterministic_reconciliation.json, model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt) and a full hash manifest are included in the submission package for reproducibility and audit.
limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates and transformation rules; this favors regular solution forms and limits generality to heterogeneous operational intents.

Shared‑initial generation semantics in confirmatory runs: the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair for seed_0; this reduces independent variability between conditions and must be considered when interpreting the paired comparison (see execution/responses/* shared‑initial files and execution/transformation_manifest.json).

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary design used one canonical seed per task (seed_0) for the paired analysis; exploratory multi‑seed analyses were preregistered but are not part of the confirmatory result presented here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces the same semantic constraints used to synthesize reference answers; this coupling increases the probability that both deterministic templates and generators closely matching the template grammar will pass, limiting construct validity for open operational distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: exact proof that the model was not exposed to template artifacts during pretraining cannot be provided; preregistered contamination heuristics (exact‑match, normalized 5‑gram overlap ≥ 0.95, normalized Levenshtein ≥ 0.90, and self‑BLEU) were computed and found no confirmatory flags (analysis/contamination_summary.csv), but residual uncertainty remains.

Single‑model, single‑validator result: findings apply to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded execution conditions and validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); they do not generalize to other LLM families, multi‑step agentic pipelines, or different validators/emulators.
